terms.gloss: a close tie, a relationship (of family, friendship or duty)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.27.2: summā necessitūdine et summā conjūnctiōne adductus
Cic. Sest. 39: sunt mihi cum illō omnēs amīcitiae necessitūdinēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a close connection, in which one person stands to another as relative or friend”. Gellius (13.3.1) reports the grammarians’ distinction: necessitās is compulsion, necessitūdō a bond. A relationship “exists between” people: intercēdit, as in multaque et magna inter nōs officia paria et mūtua intercēdunt (Cic. Fam. 13.65.1).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.65.1: mihi summa familiāritās cōnsuētūdōque est

terms.gloss: companionship, close acquaintance; (in comedy) a love affair
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.16.11: multā et jūcundā cōnsuētūdine conjūnctī inter nōs sumus
terms.comment: Also, and more often, a habit or custom.

terms.gloss: a connection, a relationship (of kinship or friendship)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.10.4: in omnibus novīs conjūnctiōnibus

phrases.latin: et hercule multā et jūcundā cōnsuētūdine conjūnctī inter nōs sumus
